later.en: This was later than France ended their rationing, and actually even later than Germany.
later.zh: 这比法国结束配给的时间晚，实际上甚至比德国还要晚。

later.en: In 1986, there was Chernobyl. And twenty-five years later, in 2011, came Fukushima.
later.zh: 1986年发生了切尔诺贝利事故。二十五年后的2011年，福岛事故又接踵而至。

law.en: It repealed the law completely, cancelling it as if it had never existed.
law.zh: 它彻底废除了这项法律，将其撤销，就像它从未存在过一样。

law.en: Belgium is one example. In 2003, Belgium passed a law committing itself to shutting down every nuclear reactor in the country.
law.zh: 比利时就是一个例子。2003年，比利时通过了一项法律，承诺关闭该国所有的核反应堆。

largely.en: At least, that's the idea. This is still new technology, largely a technology of blueprints and prototypes rather than working power stations.
largely.zh: 至少，理论上是这样的。这仍是一项新技术，在很大程度上还停留在图纸和原型阶段，而非投入实用的发电站。

largely.en: To put it in real terms, Goldman Sachs now projects that electricity demand from data centres will grow by 160% by 2030, driven largely by AI.
largely.zh: 具体来说，高盛目前预计，在人工智能的极大推动下，到2030年，数据中心的用电需求将增长160%。

layer.en: This is why fission plants need so many layers of safety systems, and those layers are a big part of what makes them so expensive to build.
layer.zh: 这就是为什么裂变电站需要层层安全系统，而这些安全系统正是造价如此高昂的主要原因。

lamb.en: Traditionally, this is eaten on Sundays, hence the name, and it involves roasted meat, chicken, pork, lamb, beef, sometimes other things like turkey as well potatoes, vegetables, gravy, Yorkshire pudding.
lamb.zh: 传统上，这在周日食用，因此得名，它包括烤肉——鸡肉、猪肉、羊肉、牛肉，有时还有火鸡等其他东西——土豆、蔬菜、肉汁、约克郡布丁。
